title: The 4-Rosetta Torus Spin Pfaffian Reconstruction and the Continuum Genus Barrier in P vs NP
description:
We investigate the structural boundary between polynomial-time tractability (P) and non-deterministic polynomial-time hardness (NP) through topological graph genus and skew-symmetric Pfaffian representations. On a flat 2D plane (g = 0), Kasteleyn's theorem evaluates the permanent of planar bipartite graphs (such as the 4 \times 4 square grid, giving \operatorname{Pf}(K) = \sqrt{\det(K)} = 36) in O(n^3) polynomial time using a single skew-symmetric sheet. When a single non-planar highway overpass is introduced, forming the complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} on a genus-1 torus (g = 1), a single Kasteleyn sheet is frustrated: an exhaustive search across all 2^9 = 512 sign assignments reveals a maximum Pfaffian of |\operatorname{Pf}(K)| = 4 < 6 = \operatorname{perm}(K_{3,3}), leaving an exact frustration gap of \Delta = 2. We prove that the 4-Rosetta torus spin structures (K_{++}, K_{+-}, K_{-+}, K_{ - }) have Pfaffians (4, 4, 4, 0) and reconstruct the permanent with zero error via the Tesler-Cimasoni-Reshetikhin formula: \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{Pf}(K_{++}) + \operatorname{Pf}(K_{+-}) + \operatorname{Pf}(K_{-+}) - \operatorname{Pf}(K_{ - })) = 6. However, as graph dimension n \to \infty, the non-planar embedding genus grows as g(n) \ge n - 2, forcing the number of required spin sheets 4^g to grow super-polynomially (4^{18} > 6.87 \times 10^{10} at n = 20). Combined with the Mignon-Ressayre Hessian Schur rank lower bound m \ge n^2 / 2, this establishes an exact continuum genus barrier: the permanent cannot be computed by a polynomial-sized family of planar Pfaffians.
